direct_answer.answer: The supplied records support that Formulation G showed a denser protective interphase and higher capacity retention after 100 cycles (92% versus 84% for the matched control). They do not by themselves establish that the denser interphase caused the retention benefit; the supplied mechanism packet provides a mechanism-consistent explanation that remains to be tested.
caveats: The reported performance comparison is limited to 100 cycles.
The causal link between interphase density, parasitic reactions, and capacity retention is not directly established by the ResearchRecords.

evidence_supported_conclusions.statement: Formulation G retained 92% capacity after 100 cycles versus 84% for the matched control.
evidence_supported_conclusions.evidence_basis: A quantitative ResearchRecord reports 92% capacity retention for Formulation G and 84% for the matched control after 100 cycles.
evidence_supported_conclusions.scope_boundary: Limited to the reported 100-cycle matched comparison; no longer-duration performance is established.
uncertainties: The supplied record does not establish whether the retention advantage persists beyond 100 cycles.

evidence_supported_conclusions.statement: Formulation G showed a denser protective interphase after 100 cycles.
evidence_supported_conclusions.evidence_basis: A characterization ResearchRecord reports a denser protective interphase after cycling.
evidence_supported_conclusions.scope_boundary: The observation is limited to the reported formulation and 100-cycle condition and does not establish causal mediation of capacity retention.
uncertainties: The ResearchRecord does not directly test whether interphase density causes lower capacity fade.
The causal role of the denser interphase in the observed retention difference is unresolved.
Transfer of the 100-cycle result to longer cycling is unknown.

evidence_gaps.gap: No supplied ResearchRecord directly tests whether the denser protective interphase mediates the capacity-retention advantage.
evidence_gaps.impact: The mechanism can inform a research direction but cannot be stated as the established cause of the performance difference.

research_leads.title: Test whether the protective interphase mediates the retention advantage
research_leads.research_question: Does the denser protective interphase observed with Formulation G reduce parasitic reactions enough to account for its higher capacity retention under matched cycling conditions?
research_leads.investigation_target: The causal relationship among protective-interphase density, parasitic-reaction activity, and capacity retention.
research_leads.rationale: The records jointly establish the interphase observation and the retention advantage, while the mechanism packet supplies a plausible link that the records do not directly verify.
boundary_conditions: conditions comparable to the reported 100-cycle result
research_leads.scientific_significance: Resolving this link would distinguish a transferable mechanism from two correlated observations in the current evidence.
uncertainties: The interphase may correlate with, rather than cause, the retention advantage.

hypotheses.title: A denser protective interphase will reduce capacity fade under matched cycling
hypotheses.statement: Under matched cycling conditions, a condition that produces a denser protective interphase will show lower parasitic-reaction activity and higher capacity retention than a lower-interphase-density control.
hypotheses.independent_variable: protective-interphase density under an otherwise matched comparison
hypotheses.expected_direction: greater protective-interphase density is associated with lower parasitic-reaction activity and higher capacity retention
hypotheses.evidence_basis: The records report a denser interphase for Formulation G and higher 100-cycle capacity retention than the matched control.
hypotheses.mechanism_reasoning: The supplied mechanism edge proposes that a dense protective interphase suppresses parasitic side reactions associated with capacity fade; this is explanatory context rather than proof.
hypotheses.falsifiable_prediction: The hypothesis is refuted if a controlled higher-interphase-density condition does not reduce parasitic-reaction activity or does not improve capacity retention relative to the lower-density control under matched cycling.
validation_conditions: use a matched control differing in the factor used to change interphase density
measure interphase density, parasitic-reaction activity, and capacity retention under the same cycling protocol
falsification_conditions: higher interphase density occurs without lower parasitic-reaction activity
higher interphase density occurs without higher capacity retention under the matched comparison
hypotheses.scientific_significance: A positive result would support a transferable interphase-mediated design principle rather than a formulation-specific association.
uncertainties: Changing interphase density may also change other cell properties that affect retention.
